**Scenario**

You are a team of public health professionals working for the City Health Department. Your city has recently experienced a significant increase in chronic health conditions (respiratory diseases, diabetes, autoimmune disorders, and cognitive decline in elderly residents). Local authorities suspect that environmental toxins may be contributing to these health problems.

Your task is to investigate the situation, identify sources of environmental toxins in your community, explain how they affect human health and propose solutions to protect the population.

Divide into groups of 4-5 students. Each team member will take on one of the following roles:

•	Toxicologist
Identify sources of environmental toxins in the community (air, water, soil, household products). Explain what toxins are present.	
Use these words: environmental toxins, pollutants, contaminants, heavy metals, industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust, pesticides, herbicides, industrial runoff, mold spores, mycotoxins
•	Public Health Doctor	
Explain how toxins affect the human body and contribute to chronic health conditions. Describe the mechanisms (oxidative stress, inflammation, endocrine disruption, neurotoxicity, immune dysregulation).	
Use these words: oxidative stress, free radicals, chronic inflammation, endocrine disruptors, mimic hormones, block hormones, neurotoxins, cognitive decline, weaken the immune system, susceptibility to infections
•	Nutritionist / Gut Health Specialist	
Explain how toxins in food and water affect the gut microbiome and digestion. Describe the consequences for overall health.	
Use these words: gut microbiome, beneficial bacteria, digestive system, increased intestinal permeability, leaky gut, inflammation throughout the body, irritable bowel syndrome, metabolic disorders
•	Community Health Advocate	
Propose practical solutions for residents to reduce their exposure to toxins. Suggest lifestyle changes, protective measures, and policy recommendations.	
Use these words: to protect oneself from heat, respiratory health, household products, cleaning supplies, cosmetics, plastics, to contaminate soil and water, to accumulate in the body, toxic effects
•	Medical Researcher	
Present evidence on how toxins are linked to specific chronic diseases (cardiovascular disease, diabetes, autoimmune disorders, neurodegenerative diseases). Explain the importance of research and statistics.	
Use these words: chronic health conditions, neurodegenerative diseases, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, autoimmune disorders, cumulative effects, trigger, exacerbate

*Work as a team. Read the information below about your city and discuss:*
1. Which environmental toxins are present in your community?
2. What are the potential sources?
3. Which health problems might be linked to these toxins?
